newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-Coates rated a buy.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-Coates rated a buy.

text.p: Morgan Stockbroking Ltd said it was recommending newly-listed equipment hire group Coates Hire Ltd as a buy, reflecting good growth prospects.
"The company is attractively priced based on 1997 fundamentals," analyst John Clifford said in a report.
"Coates has a well-recognised brand name and good growth prospects," Clifford said.
Implementation of a growth strategy based on diversification and a general recovery in construction activity had delivered improved results in the past three years, the report said.
"Forecasts of higher non-dwelling and engineering construction, and a continued trend towards outsourcing provides a buoyant outlook for earnings," it said.

Coates, listed this month after the sale of Australian National Industries Ltd's 100 percent holding, had a balance sheet "comfortably geared" at 46 percent and interest cover forecast to rise to eight times in the year ended June 30, 1997 from 6.7 times in 1995/96, Clifford said.
The Coates prospectus had forecast sales growth of 12 percent to A$124.6 million in 1996/97 and higher margins translating to earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) of $24 million, up 24 percent.
"With a positive outlook for construction in Australia, Coates is attractively priced at a price-earnings ratio of 11 times," Clifford said.
Coates customer base of more than 30,000 was extensive with the company's recent focus to develop closer links with the larger users, Clifford said.
Coates had also positioned itself in the Indonesian market ahead of anticipated strong growth in demand due to high levels of infrastructure development, the report said.
Coates shares were issued at A$2.00.
In late trading on Monday the stock was trading at A$2.26.
